tasks.title: Reproject points from WGS84 to UTM 37S
tasks.prompt: The table `t01_points` holds 3 points in EPSG:4326 (lon/lat) near Nairobi. Reproject them to the appropriate UTM zone for this area (EPSG:32737) and return id + geometry in that CRS.

candidates.name: correct
candidates.label: correct
candidates.description: ST_Transform reprojects the coordinates into EPSG:32737.
candidates.detail: [crs_check] output CRS EPSG:32737 (expected EPSG:32737) ; [vector_equiv] all 3 features match within 1.0 m
candidates.solution_code:
-- Correct: ST_Transform actually reprojects the coordinates into EPSG:32737.
SELECT id, ST_AsGeoJSON(ST_Transform(geom, 32737)) AS geojson
FROM t01_points
ORDER BY id;

candidates.name: wrong_assign_srid
candidates.label: wrong
candidates.description: Relabeled the CRS to 32737 (ST_SetSRID) but never transformed the coordinates — they are still lon/lat degrees.
candidates.solution_code:
-- BUG (the classic -a_srs vs -t_srs / "define vs reproject" trap):
-- ST_SetSRID only RELABELS the CRS metadata to 32737; the coordinates are still
-- lon/lat degrees. The layer now CLAIMS to be UTM but never moved — it lines up
-- with nothing. crs_check passes (label is right) but vector_equiv fails.
SELECT id, ST_AsGeoJSON(ST_SetSRID(geom, 32737)) AS geojson
FROM t01_points
ORDER BY id;

candidates.name: wrong_utm_zone
candidates.label: wrong
candidates.description: Reprojected to the wrong UTM zone (EPSG:32736 instead of 32737).
candidates.detail: [crs_check] output CRS EPSG:32736 (expected EPSG:32737) ; [vector_equiv] CRS mismatch: candidate EPSG:32736 vs golden EPSG:32737 (coordinates were not reprojected to the target CRS)

tasks.title: Total area of 1 km sensor buffers
tasks.prompt: The table `t02_points` holds 3 points in EPSG:4326 near Nairobi. Compute the SUM of the areas of a 1 km buffer around each point, in square metres.

candidates.name: correct
candidates.label: correct
candidates.description: Buffers on geography (metres) and sums ST_Area in m².

candidates.name: wrong_degrees
candidates.label: wrong
candidates.description: Buffered in degrees on a 4326 layer; ST_Area returned square degrees (~7.6e-4) instead of m².
candidates.solution_code:
-- BUG (the #1 silent GIS failure): the layer is EPSG:4326, so this buffers by
-- ~0.009 DEGREES (a naive "1 km ≈ 0.009°" conversion) and ST_Area then returns
-- SQUARE DEGREES, not square metres. The query runs fine and returns a tiny
-- number ~7.6e-4 instead of ~9.4e6.
SELECT SUM(ST_Area(ST_Buffer(geom, 0.009)))::float AS value
FROM t02_points;

tasks.title: Assign each sensor its containing zone
tasks.prompt: Tables `t03_sensors` (points) and `t03_zones` (polygons) are both in EPSG:4326. For each sensor return its id and the id of the zone that CONTAINS it (0 if it is inside no zone).

candidates.name: correct
candidates.label: correct
candidates.description: ST_Contains point-in-polygon with a LEFT JOIN; outside points map to 0.
candidates.solution_code:
-- Correct: ST_Contains tests actual point-in-polygon; a LEFT JOIN keeps sensors
-- that fall in no zone, and COALESCE maps them to 0.
SELECT s.id AS id,
       COALESCE(z.id, 0) AS zone_id,
       ST_AsGeoJSON(s.geom) AS geojson
FROM t03_sensors s
LEFT JOIN t03_zones z ON ST_Contains(z.geom, s.geom)
ORDER BY s.id;

candidates.name: wrong_nearest
candidates.label: wrong
candidates.description: Assigned the nearest zone instead of the containing zone; sensor 3 (outside all zones) was wrongly assigned zone 2.
candidates.solution_code:
-- BUG: uses the NEAREST zone (<-> distance operator) instead of the CONTAINING
-- zone. Every sensor gets a zone — including sensor 3, which is outside every
-- polygon and should be 0. Geometry matches the golden; the zone_id attribute
-- is wrong, so vector_equiv (check_attrs: zone_id) catches it.
SELECT s.id AS id,
       (SELECT z.id FROM t03_zones z ORDER BY z.geom <-> s.geom LIMIT 1) AS zone_id,
       ST_AsGeoJSON(s.geom) AS geojson
FROM t03_sensors s
ORDER BY s.id;

tasks.title: Sensors within 500 m of a target
tasks.prompt: Table `t04_sensors` is in EPSG:4326. Return the ids of all sensors within 500 metres of the point (lon 36.81, lat -1.29). Use an index-aware, metric-correct distance test.

candidates.name: correct
candidates.label: correct
candidates.description: ST_DWithin on geography: metric and index-aware. Returns {1,3}.
candidates.solution_code:
-- Correct: ST_DWithin on geography measures METRES and is index-aware (the GiST
-- index on geom is used via the spheroid bbox). Returns sensors 1 and 3.
SELECT s.id AS id
FROM t04_sensors s
WHERE ST_DWithin(s.geom::geography,
                 ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(36.81, -1.29), 4326)::geography,
                 500)
ORDER BY s.id;

candidates.name: wrong_distance_degrees
candidates.label: wrong
candidates.description: ST_Distance < 500 on a 4326 geometry compares in degrees (matches everything) and defeats the GiST index. Returns {1,2,3,4}.
candidates.detail: [sql_result] result set differs: 0 missing e.g. [], 2 extra e.g. [(2,), (4,)]
candidates.solution_code:
-- BUG: ST_Distance on geometry in EPSG:4326 returns DEGREES, so "< 500" means
-- "within 500 degrees" — i.e. everything on Earth. It also cannot use the GiST
-- index (a function on the column forces a sequential scan). Returns all 4 ids.
SELECT s.id AS id
FROM t04_sensors s
WHERE ST_Distance(s.geom, ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(36.81, -1.29), 4326)) < 500
ORDER BY s.id;

tasks.title: City-wide sensor density (unanswerable)

tasks.rejection_reason: The zones layer covers only the south-west quadrant of the study area, and no city/metropolitan boundary layer is provided. A city-wide density cannot be computed from partial-coverage data without inventing the denominator.

tasks.title: Publish zones and read them back over WFS
tasks.prompt: Publish the `zones` PostGIS layer in GeoServer (workspace `geoeval`) and return the number of features a WFS 2.0 GetFeature returns for the bbox covering all zones.

candidates.name: correct
candidates.label: correct
candidates.description: Publishes the layer and queries WFS 2.0 with a CRS-qualified bbox (urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::4326), getting all 4 zones.

candidates.name: wrong_axis_order
candidates.label: wrong
candidates.description: Passed the bbox as minx,miny,maxx,maxy without a CRS URI. WFS 2.0 / EPSG:4326 expects lat,lon (Y,X) axis order, so the bbox lands in the ocean and returns 0 features.
